phase_name: Wire, Deploy, and Run the Full Gate Set

objectives.description: Hand-verify every authored file against manifest.json provides.*
Load the approvals extension into this repository (manager.load) and resync all active extensions
Close gate 3 Rule E / deploy-drift and gate 5 manifest-parity findings via resync
Close gate 20 (eager-context budget) overage: trim EXTENSION.md to its floor, then a deliberate, documented baseline_bytes move
Run the complete, unnarrowed verify-deploy.sh (all 21 gates)

approaches_tried.approach: trim EXTENSION.md prose repeatedly to close the gate-20 eager-context overage without touching the shared budget config
approaches_tried.reason: Compressed EXTENSION.md from 1725 B to a 105 B structural floor (heading + one clause + README.md pointer, smaller than every other extension's own CLAUDE.md entry) and the overage only shrank from 1715 B to 95 B -- it never reached zero, because the baseline's own pre-existing headroom was already only ~9 B (65941/65950) before this task started. Any new extension's unavoidable minimal CLAUDE.md footprint exceeds that. Closed instead by a deliberate, dated eager_load.baseline_bytes move (65950 -> 66100) with a full derivation note, after concluding the alternative (omitting /approve's CLAUDE.md entry, making it undiscoverable) was worse -- see issue-record.sh entry and phase-9 handoff for the full reasoning.

deviations.description: eager_load.baseline_bytes in agent-system/extensions/core/context/config/orchestrator-context-budget.json was moved from 65950 to 66100
deviations.reason: This file's own history (5 consecutive prior entries) established a strict 'always trim, never bump' culture for this specific field. This task deviates from that culture, on the judgment that a 105 B structural floor for a brand-new, required, discoverable command entry has no further redistributable slack -- unlike every prior overage, which was bloat creep in content this repository already carried. Recorded as an issue (gate-collision, severity costly) flagging this as a structural tension for future review rather than a routine, silently-accepted precedent break.
